knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What is the maximum-likelihood construction move? (2) Why is the log-likelihood often maximised instead? (3) How does this differ from method of moments?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Maximum likelihood chooses the parameter value that maximises the likelihood (equivalently the log-likelihood under regularity). MoM matches moments; MLE maximises the model likelihood.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. IID claims X₁,…,Xₙ ~ Exponential with rate λ (pdf λ e^{−λx} for x>0). (1) Write the log-likelihood for λ and state the MLE. (2) Refuse: 'Yesterday's method-of-moments estimator is the same skill as maximum likelihood.'
knowledge_checks.body: Form and maximise likelihood; refuse MoM-as-MLE.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MLE is defined by maximising the likelihood; moment matching is a different estimator construction.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) ℓ(λ) = n ln λ − λ Σ xᵢ; MLE λ̂ = n/Σ xᵢ = 1/x̄. (2) Refuse: MoM matches moments; MLE maximises the likelihood (or log-likelihood). Different construction — even when numerical answers coincide.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing MoM and MLE because they sometimes give the same number.
success_criteria: Forms log-likelihood and states the MLE for the Exponential rate.
Refuses treating MoM as the same skill as MLE.
